title: Pore-Induced Stress Concentration Driving Crack Propagation
introduction: During electrophoretic deposition (EPD) of TiO2 photoanode coatings for dye-sensitized solar cells, bubble formation near the deposition electrode creates pores in the deposited layer. These pores remain embedded in the TiO2 coating after deposition and act as stress concentration sites during post-deposition drying and thermal treatment. Stress concentrations around the pore tips drive crack propagation through the TiO2 coating, producing crack networks that compromise the continuity and photocurrent collection of the photoanode layer.
reasoning: The 697-Elsevier EPD study explicitly identifies pore-induced stress concentration as the mechanism by which bubble-formed porosity drives crack propagation in TiO2 coatings, linking it directly to cracking failure and efficiency loss.
